instruction.text: Read the text. Decide if the following statements are true or false.

atoms.text:
1976: The Grunwick Strikes

In August 1976, a group of predominantly South Asian women (many of them refugees who had fled Uganda and Kenya) walked out of the Grunwick Film Processing Laboratories in northwest London. They were protesting against low wages, compulsory overtime and the dismissal of a colleague.
atoms.sound: In August 1976, a group of predominantly South Asian women (many of them refugees who had fled Uganda and Kenya) walked out of the Grunwick Film Processing Laboratories in northwest London. They were protesting against low wages, compulsory overtime and the dismissal of a colleague.

atoms.a: The Grunwick strike began in August 1976.
The workers were protesting against unsafe working conditions in the factory.

wrong.text: They were protesting against low wages, compulsory overtime and the dismissal of a colleague.

atoms.a: Many of the strikers were South Asian women who had previously fled Uganda and Kenya.

atoms.text: Their strike, which lasted nearly two years, became one of the most significant labour disputes in British history. The image of these women (sometimes described as “strikers in saris”) standing on the picket line challenged stereotypes about both South Asian women and migrant workers.

atoms.b:
2018: The Windrush Scandal

In 2018, it became known that hundreds of people from the Windrush Generation had arrived in Britain completely ((legally)) in the 1950s and 1960s, yet were being treated as if they had no right to remain.

Because many had arrived as children on their parents' passports, they lacked the documentation to prove their right ((to_stay)). The situation was made worse when the Home Office admitted it had destroyed thousands of ((landing_cards)) belonging to Windrush arrivals in 2010.

The root cause was the government's “((hostile_environment))” policy, which required landlords, employers, banks and the National Health Service (NHS) to check people's immigration ((status)) before providing services or employment.

As a result, many Windrush arrivals were wrongly ((detained)) by authorities, denied access to healthcare, lost their jobs or were threatened with being ((deported)) to countries they had left decades earlier.

Following the public outcry, Home Secretary Amber Rudd ((resigned)) from her position. The government was forced to establish a ((compensation)) scheme for those affected. Many victims, however, reported that claiming it remained extremely difficult.
